data.comment: The label of the "Global Catalog Server" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Global_Catalog_Server_Description
data.value: Applies to Active Directory. The Global Catalog server JIM searches when it probes for a value already in use that must be unique across the whole forest (userPrincipalName, servicePrincipalName, mail and proxyAddresses), so a value held in another domain is found. JIM connects on port 3268, or 3269 with LDAPS, with the credentials below. When left blank, JIM uses the domain controller it connects to, if that is a Global Catalog and the forest has more than one domain. For LDAPS, use a name present in the server's certificate.
data.comment: The description of the "Global Catalog Server" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.value: Maximum number of parallel LDAP connections used during full imports from OpenLDAP, 389 Directory Server and Generic directories. Each connection handles one container and object type combination independently, avoiding RFC 2696 paging cookie limitations. Not used for Active Directory. Default is 4. Recommended range: 2-8.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Include_Auxiliary_Classes_Description
data.value: Applies to Active Directory only. When enabled, auxiliary object classes are included in schema discovery alongside structural classes. Enable this if you need to import or export objects whose primary class is declared as auxiliary in the directory schema. RFC 4512 directories (OpenLDAP, 389 Directory Server) always discover auxiliary classes, because JIM merges the ones an administrator selects into the structural Object Type they extend.
data.comment: The description of the "Include Auxiliary Classes" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Skip_Hidden_Partitions_Description

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Export_Settings_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Export Settings" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Export_Concurrency_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Export Concurrency" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Export_Concurrency_Description
data.value: Maximum number of concurrent LDAP operations during export. Higher values improve throughput but increase load on the target directory. Left at the default of 4, JIM raises it on schema import: to 16 for Active Directory and 389 Directory Server, and to 8 for OpenLDAP, which then sends 4 batches at once rather than 2. Samba AD and other directories stay at 4.
data.comment: The description of the "Export Concurrency" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Modify_Batch_Size_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Modify Batch Size" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Modify_Batch_Size_Description
data.value: Maximum number of values per multi-valued attribute modification in a single LDAP request. When adding or removing many values from a multi-valued attribute (e.g., group members), changes are split into batches of this size. Lower values improve compatibility with constrained LDAP servers; higher values improve throughput, especially for very large groups. Default is 1000. Recommended range: 100-2000.
data.comment: The description of the "Modify Batch Size" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Manage_Exchange_recipients_Description
data.value: Active Directory only. Makes the objects this Connected System provisions Exchange recipients (mailboxes, mail users, mail contacts and mail-enabled groups), as declared by the Exchange attributes their Synchronisation Rules flow.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Exchange_server_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Exchange server" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector.

data.name: JIM_LDAP_Connector_Exchange_server_Description
data.value: The Exchange server JIM signs in to, as the account above, to create and update recipients: its host name, such as ex1.panoply.local, or its full remote PowerShell address. A host name uses http, where Kerberos encrypts the session; for an https:// address, add the certificate authority that issued the server's certificate in Certificates. JIM works out the Kerberos sign-in from the directory settings.
data.comment: The description of the "Exchange server" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.value: Placeholder member DN used for group object classes that require at least one member (e.g. groupOfNames). When a group has no real members, this value is added to satisfy the schema constraint. It is automatically filtered out during import. Only applies to non-AD directories. Default: cn=placeholder. If your directory has referential integrity enabled, set this to an existing entry's DN.
data.comment: The description of the "Group Placeholder Member DN" setting of the JIM LDAP Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.comment: The label of the "Object Types" setting of the JIM SQL Connector.

data.name: JIM_SQL_Connector_Object_Types_Description
data.value: Which Connected System Object Types this database holds, and where each one's objects come from, as a JSON document. Each object type needs a 'name' and 'anchorColumns' (the column or columns whose values identify a row), and exactly one source: a 'table' (a table or a view, optionally qualified with a 'schema') or a 'select' statement where a view cannot be created. 'columns' declares what a column's type cannot say, which today means naming the object type a column's values point at ('referencesObjectType'); JIM never guesses that from a foreign key, but it does suggest one where the database declares it. 'relatedTables' turns a table of one row per value into a multi-valued attribute: name the attribute, its 'valueColumn', and the 'joinColumns' that join a row back to its parent (one per anchor column, in the same order), plus 'referencesObjectType' where those values are references, as group membership is. Every other column is discovered and typed automatically. The example below is a complete document to start from.
data.comment: The description of the "Object Types" setting of the JIM SQL Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_SQL_Connector_Delta_Import_Mode_Description
data.value: How a Delta Import finds out what has changed. Leave it unset where this Connected System only runs Full Imports. 'Change-Log Table' reads a table or view your database keeps, with one row per change. It is the recommended mode, and the only one that sees a deletion. 'Watermark Column' reads a last-modified or version column on each table. It needs nothing added to the database, but sees only creates and updates, so deletions are found by a Full Import. Each Object Type then names its change-log table or its watermark columns, on its card above (in the Object Types document, 'changeLog' or 'watermarkColumn').

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Authentication_Method_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Authentication Method" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Authentication_Method_Description
data.value: How JIM proves it is the app registration. A certificate, as Microsoft Entra Connect now uses, is recommended: its private key never leaves JIM, whereas a client secret is sent with every token request. A federated credential holds no secret at all: where JIM runs on an Azure virtual machine with a user-assigned managed identity, the app registration trusts that identity's token instead. Use a client secret for a quick trial.
data.comment: The description of the "Authentication Method" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Authentication_Method_Option_Certificate
data.comment: A choice of the "Authentication Method" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector. The English text is what is stored; this is only how it reads.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Certificate_Description
data.value: The certificate and its private key, as a PFX file's contents Base64-encoded, i.e. the output of [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('app.pfx')) in PowerShell. Upload the same certificate (without its private key) under Certificates & secrets on the app registration. It needs an RSA key of at least 2048 bits.
data.comment: The description of the "Certificate" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Managed_Identity_Client_ID_Description

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Connection_Timeout_Description
data.value: How long to wait, in seconds, for Microsoft Graph or the token service to answer a request before giving up. Up to 600.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Rate_Limiting_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Rate Limiting" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Maximum_Writes_Per_Second_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Maximum Writes Per Second" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Maximum_Writes_Per_Second_Description
data.value: The most writes JIM sends to the tenant each second, from 1 to 20. Microsoft Graph allows each application 20 writes a second in a tenant, and every application in the tenant shares a wider limit, so the default of 10 leaves room for the tenant's other applications. JIM slows down further by itself while Graph reports the tenant is near its limit. Reads are not limited here; JIM waits whenever Graph asks it to.
data.comment: The description of the "Maximum Writes Per Second" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Maximum_Retries_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Maximum Retries" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Maximum_Retries_Description
data.value: How many times to retry a request that failed for a temporary reason, such as throttling (HTTP 429) or Graph being briefly unavailable, from 0 to 10. JIM waits as long as Graph asks before each retry.
data.comment: The description of the "Maximum Retries" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Source_of_Authority_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Source of Authority" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Track_Source_of_Authority_Changes_Label
data.comment: The label of the "Track Source of Authority Changes" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector.

data.name: JIM_Microsoft_Entra_ID_Connector_Track_Source_of_Authority_Changes_Description
data.value: Whether to read, for each object synchronised from Active Directory, whether its Source of Authority has been switched to Entra ID, or switched back, so sourceOfAuthority shows where it is managed now. Turn it on in a hybrid tenant whose objects have their Source of Authority switched. It needs the User-OnPremisesSyncBehavior.ReadWrite.All and Group-OnPremisesSyncBehavior.ReadWrite.All permissions, the only ones Microsoft offers for reading it, which also allow changing it. Off, an object synchronised from Active Directory always reads as onPremisesDirectory.
data.comment: The description of the "Track Source of Authority Changes" setting of the JIM Microsoft Entra ID Connector, shown under the field. Setting names it mentions stay in English: they are the names the REST API and PowerShell use.

data.name: JIM_File_Connector_Group_Object_Type
data.comment: The heading above settings of which exactly one must be filled in (the File Connector's Object Type group). The English text is the group's name in the Connector.

data.name: JIM_SCIM_2_0_Service_Provider_Connector_ConnectorDescription
data.value: Lets SCIM 2.0 clients provision into JIM. JIM acts as the SCIM service provider: clients write Users and Groups to JIM's own SCIM endpoint, and this Connector imports what they wrote.
data.comment: The description of the SCIM 2.0 Service Provider Connector, on the Connectors page. Users and Groups are SCIM resource types.
